title: The district report that did not add up
instructions:
## You are the district health information officer

The regional office has queried last month's malaria figures: confirmed cases entered in DHIS2 exceed the number of tests done. Examine the evidence, find the cause and fix the process, not just the number.

nodes.title: What is wrong?
nodes.text: Regional query: "Confirmed malaria cases (1,240) exceed tests performed (980) for Akyem West, October."

evidence.title: DHIS2 entry for October
evidence.text: Oda Hospital. Suspected: 1,900. Tests: 980. Confirmed: 1,240. Treated with ACT: 1,250.

evidence.title: Facility tally sheet
evidence.text: RDT done: 760. Microscopy done: 220. Positive (RDT): 410. Positive (microscopy): 70. Treated: 1,250 (includes 770 treated on clinical judgement without a test).

evidence.title: Data element definitions
evidence.text: "Confirmed malaria case" = positive by RDT or microscopy. Untested treated patients are reported as "presumed", never as "confirmed".

choices.text: The tests count was under-entered; raise it to match
choices.feedback: The tally sheet confirms 980 tests; the cases figure is wrong.

choices.text: Untested treated patients were entered as confirmed cases
choices.feedback: Correct. 410 + 70 = 480 confirmed; the rest came from the treated-without-test group.

nodes.title: Which quality dimension?
nodes.text: Which data quality dimension does this belong to?

choices.feedback: The report arrived on time; the content is wrong.
Correct. The value does not match the data element's definition.

choices.text: Correct the entry to 480 confirmed and 770 presumed, with a note, and verify at the facility
choices.feedback: Correct. Fix from the source document and keep an audit note.
Deleting data destroys the audit trail.

choices.text: Ask the facility to re-count patients in the ward
choices.feedback: The counts exist; the classification is the problem.

nodes.title: Stop it happening again
nodes.text: The same error happened twice this year. What prevents the third time?

choices.text: A DHIS2 validation rule (confirmed ≤ tests) flagged at entry, plus a refresher for the records officer
choices.feedback: Correct. The rule catches it at entry; training fixes the understanding.
Blame without a tool rarely changes data.

choices.text: Hand-checking every facility monthly at the district
choices.feedback: That does not scale and is a month late.

nodes.title: The deeper problem
nodes.text: 770 patients were treated without a test. What does that tell the director?

choices.text: Nothing; treating on symptoms is normal
Probably an RDT stock-out or staffing gap that needs a supply or supervision response
choices.feedback: Correct. The data problem revealed a service problem, which is what the system is for.
The tally sheet records real patients.

nodes.title: Query answered
nodes.text: You reply with corrected figures, the cause, the new validation rule and a note that Oda Hospital needs RDT supplies.

hints: Compare the confirmed figure with the positives on the tally sheet.
Accuracy is whether the value matches the definition.
The best fixes happen at the point of entry.

checks.label: You read the tally sheet and the definitions
At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: DHIS2 validation rules and the WHO Data Quality Review toolkit formalise these checks; district officers in Ghana run them monthly before submission.
